previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with HCV-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for observation following radiofrequency ablation of liver lesions in segments 8 and 5, along with therapeutic drainage of 5 liters of ascites. The procedure was performed under general anesthesia and was uncomplicated, though the initial ascitic fluid was slightly bloody, prompting overnight monitoring. Serial hemoglobin and hematocrit levels remained stable, and mild hyponatremia (Na 130) was managed with albumin infusion. The patient’s pain was controlled with oxycodone, and he remained hemodynamically stable throughout. He was discharged home with instructions to continue home medications, use oxycodone as needed for pain, and follow up with his primary care provider for repeat labs and hepatology for a CT scan in four weeks.

#Post-RFA syndrome:
CT scan of abdomen and pelvis showed post-RFA changes, but no 
evidence of intrahepatic pseudo aneurysm or retroperitoneal 
hematoma. CXR showed interval development of right pleural 
effusion and possible infiltrate, so the patient was started on 
levofloxacin for treatment of possible community-acquired 
pneumonia.  Interventional Radiology was consulted, who felt 
that his clinical and imaging findings were most consistent with 
soft tissue hematoma, possibly related to a small 
pseudo-aneurysm in the RF probe insertion soft tissue tract. 
This appeared to have been self-limited as labs were stable.  
Patient remained afebrile during hospitalization and 
hemodynamically stable.  Patient discharged with a plan to 
complete treatment for CAP with levofloxacin (last day of 
antibiotic ___.

now cured s/p sofosbuvir and ribavirin).  Complicated by history 
of esophageal varices, hepatic encephalopathy, and ascites. He 
also has HCC as above. No signs of decompensation on admission,  
and his ascites and encephalopathy are well-controlled.  
Thrombocytopenia at baseline.

to 127.  The patient 
has a history of intermittent hyponatremia. The patient received

INDICATION:  History: ___ with s/p recent ablation of liverNO_PO contrast  //
multiphasic. ?pseudoaneurysm

TECHNIQUE:  Multiphasic Liver: Multidetector CT of the abdomen and pelvis was
done as part of CT torso without and with IV contrast. Initially, the abdomen
was scanned without IV contrast. Subsequently, images of the abdomen were
obtained in the early arterial phase, followed by images of the abdomen and
pelvis in the portal venous phase, followed by images of the abdomen in
equilibrium phase (3-min delay). IV Contrast:  130 mL Omnipaque.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.
Oral contrast was not administered.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 1,759 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis dated ___, MRI liver dated ___

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: There is a large right, simple pleural effusion with associated
compressive atelectasis.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver contour is nodular and dysmorphic, consistent with
the patient's underlying cirrhosis.  The previously noted segment VII lesion
that has undergone prior chemoembolization retains ethidol.  There is stable
postablative appearance of the segment VI lesion as well.  There are post
radiofrequency ablation changes in the segment V lesion.  No intrahepatic
pseudo aneurysm is identified.  Numerous calcified gallstones are seen within
the collapsed gallbladder.  There is no gallbladder wall thickening.  Moderate
free fluid is noted.   The portal vein and its branches are patent, though the
posterior branch of the right portal vein is attenuated.

PANCREAS: A number of sub 5 mm hypodense lesions are seen in the head and
uncinate process of the pancreas, unchanged since prior examinations, likely
benign.  These are better characterized on recent MRI.

SPLEEN: The spleen is enlarged measuring up to 15.5 cm in greatest dimension. 
No focal splenic lesions are identified.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: A simple cyst is noted in the right kidney.  Otherwise the kidneys
are unremarkable.  There is no hydronephrosis or perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  There are
numerous colonic diverticuli without evidence of acute diverticulitis.  The
appendix is normal.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: The aorta and its branches are heavily calcified.  Again noted is
significant narrowing of the right renal artery at its origin.  There are
extensive periesophageal varices and periumbilical varices.  The umbilical
vein is recanalized.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or
acute fracture.  There is asymmetric body wall edema, worse on the right than
on the left.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of intrahepatic pseudo aneurysm or retroperitoneal hematoma.
2. Post radiofrequency ablation changes in the liver.
3. Findings consistent with cirrhosis and portal hypertension including
nodular liver contours, simple appearing ascites, splenomegaly, and varices.
4. Assymetric body wall edema, worse on the right.
